title: Profile canonical TypedRelationBlock validation cost without adding a trusted constructor
question: GPU-10 showed canonical TypedRelationBlock construction dominating packed Boolean materialization. Which existing canonical validation frames account for that cost before any production fast path is considered?

change.unprofiled_baseline: Retain separate unprofiled constructor samples because cProfile observer overhead changes absolute timings.
change.reuse: Reuse the existing ProbeCase fixture, packed Boolean primitives, canonical block factory, sampling helper, Fourfold subject, and existing Fourfold/Tensor workflow.

frozen_diagnostic.measurement_caveat: cProfile self/cumulative timings include observer overhead and are non-additive; unprofiled construction medians are the wall-time baseline.

finding.summary: The dominant profiled construction work is the repeated generic any/generator validation surface inside TypedRelationBlock.__post_init__, not bounded-sequence admission, semiring resolution, or identifier admission.
finding.largest_case: At 256/0.05 and 43,264 output entries, unprofiled canonical construction was 12.517520 ms median. Under cProfile, __post_init__ accumulated 45.741211 ms; builtin any accumulated 30.820779 ms across 260 calls and nested validation generators accumulated 20.125544 ms across 130,309 calls. These cumulative figures overlap and must not be summed.
finding.structural_signal: builtin any call count is row-count plus four in the 64/128/256 cases, matching four whole-array validation predicates plus one strict-order predicate per row; generator work grows with rows and stored entries.
finding.negative_result: The evidence does not justify a trusted constructor, cache, alternate relation representation, or another arithmetic backend.

next_implication: A subsequent bounded packet may test one fused canonical CSR validation pass inside TypedRelationBlock.__post_init__ that preserves every current fail-closed invariant while reducing repeated whole-array/per-row scans. It must prove invalid-input parity and canonical digest parity before any timing claim.
